clue.text: Corrective final word offered by US lawyer to politician

parts.note: Amen is the word said at the close of a prayer
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: An American lawyer's last word to a politician puts things right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amendatory serves to amend or correct, so it is corrective in nature.

clue.text: Month in which drama academy is set up

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the word is written upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London

explanation.surface: A month during which a drama school is founded.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar is a month of the Jewish calendar, falling around February and March.

clue.text: The first person set free, having climbed fencing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the pieces are read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: the first person is number one, written NO plus the digit 1 as I
to save someone is to rescue or set them free

explanation.surface: The first prisoner released after scaling the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests a barrier, but here it means verbal fencing: parrying questions. NO I + SAVE reads NOISAVE, which 'having climbed' turns upwards into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing in argument means sparring and dodging questions, which is evasion.

clue.text: An action that leaves the head isolated

definitions.text: An action that leaves the head isolated

parts.words: An action that leaves the head isolated
parts.note: read literally, an act which leaves someone's head on its own, cut off from the body, rather than a leader left lonely

explanation.definitionFit: Beheading severs the head from the body, leaving it entirely separated.

clue.text: Playing a sort of sound that's exciting for O'Reilly?

definitions.meaning: producing a quavering, warbling musical sound, as a bird or a flute does
an Irishman like O'Reilly is supposed to drop the H after T, so a word for exciting comes out without it

explanation.walkthrough: The joke rests on the stereotyped Irish pronunciation in which 'th' sounds like 't' ('tree' for 'three'), so thrilling loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A trill is a rapid alternation of notes, so trilling is making that warbling sound.

clue.text: Pole drinking cask of booze becomes corpulent

indicators.note: the pole takes the cask inside it, as a drinker takes in drink

parts.note: a rod is a pole
a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A Pole who downs a whole barrel of drink grows fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality, but it is just a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund describes someone plump and round, a synonym of corpulent.

clue.text: Wartime food plans suffering a setback

indicators.note: a setback sends the word back, so it is read from the end

parts.note: maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: Wartime food schemes go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam, the tinned pork luncheon meat, was a staple of British rationing in the Second World War.

clue.text: Writer with weapon bagging one bird

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: the weapon bags, i.e. holds within it, the next piece

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A writer armed with a gun shoots a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bagging' sounds like a hunter's kill, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A penguin is a flightless seabird of the southern hemisphere.

clue.text: They may provide many openings in the hotel business

definitions.text: They may provide many openings in the hotel business

parts.words: They may provide many openings in the hotel business
parts.note: read as job opportunities in hospitality, but literally things that open many hotel room doors

explanation.definitionFit: A hotel's master key opens every room lock, so it gives access to many doors.

clue.text: Cunning is evident in workers who want to bust the Government?

definitions.text: who want to bust the Government?

indicators.note: the cunning is seen sitting inside the workers

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers
arch means sly or roguish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Workers plotting to bring down the government are showing their craftiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' reads as the definition's subject, but it only supplies the ants; the definition is the description of what such people want.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchists seek to abolish organized government altogether, so they want to see it brought down.

clue.text: Aims to make repairs when the front's fallen off

indicators.note: losing its front means the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: mends means repairs, makes good

explanation.surface: Someone intends to fix something after its front has broken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends in the sense of goals or purposes are one's aims.

clue.text: It could involve Monsieur messing about with Dame

definitions.text: It could involve Monsieur messing about with Dame

indicators.note: messing about signals that the letters are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman fooling around with a titled lady could be a minor offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the jumbled letters of MONSIEUR and DAME, and the bad conduct their dalliance suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdemeanour is a minor wrongdoing, which illicit fooling around could well be.

clue.text: Learner, trouble-maker being slack

parts.note: L is the learner driver plate in the UK
an imp is a mischievous troublemaker

explanation.surface: A mischievous learner is being lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means lacking firmness, hanging loose, which is slack.

clue.text: Outing led astray? Find this on a map

indicators.note: led astray here means the letters are taken off course and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An outing that went the wrong way, so check the map.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of longitude, east or west of Greenwich, are marked on maps and globes.

clue.text: Trained spies prove to be overpowering

indicators.note: trained here means the letters are drilled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trained spies turn out to be overwhelming.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppressive weather or rule is crushing and overpowering.

clue.text: Awfully inept part of hospital feeling bad about things

indicators.note: awfully suggests the next word is badly done and so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy on a hospital ward feels guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A penitent person feels remorse for wrongdoing, i.e. bad about what they did.

clue.text: Man's entering Greek city (where not all speak Greek!)

indicators.note: the man's piece goes into the abbreviation for Greek

parts.note: Dan is a man's name, so Man's gives DAN'S

explanation.surface: A man enters a Greek city, though few there speak Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside is a joke: Gdansk is a Polish city, so hardly anyone speaks Greek there.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a major Polish port city on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: What may destroy some evidence when mum gets more embarrassed

parts.note: mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence
someone more embarrassed blushes redder

explanation.surface: Evidence gets destroyed while Mother grows ever more flushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother, but it is the call for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A shredder cuts documents into strips, often used to get rid of incriminating papers.

clue.text: Tell member of the family, one against missing out

indicators.note: missing out means these letters are left out of the word

parts.note: a relative is a family member
I is the Roman numeral one
V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Tell a relation that one opponent has been left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it.

clue.text: More than one vehicle is still, including old Rolls-Royce

indicators.note: the first piece includes, i.e. contains, the next

parts.note: something that lies is still and inert

explanation.surface: Several vehicles are parked, including a vintage Rolls-Royce.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorries are large goods vehicles, the British word for trucks, so the plural fits.

clue.text: Companion goes to little woman carrying garment material

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: the little woman carries the garment inside her

parts.note: Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women
a bra is an undergarment

explanation.surface: A friend visits a young woman carrying fabric for clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garment material' looks like one phrase; the garment is BRA, and material alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambray is a light cotton fabric woven with white weft on a coloured warp.

clue.text: Poem starts to read oddly, Auden being 'off'?

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the next words are taken
off means out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poem begins to read strangely when Auden is not on form.
explanation.walkthrough: W H Auden, the poet, fits the surface so well that his name hardly looks like fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French verse form with a recurring refrain.

clue.text: Capital providing volunteers to go round country

indicators.note: the volunteers surround the country piece

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
Iran is a country

explanation.surface: A capital supplies volunteers to tour the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital city of Albania.

clue.text: Preach to get one remiss sorted out

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lecture to get a negligent person straightened out.
explanation.definitionFit: To sermonise is to deliver a sermon, i.e. to preach or moralise.

clue.text: One of the family has a superior set of books

parts.note: taken as written
U denotes upper-class, superior
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A relative owns a fine set of books.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, so she is a relative.

clue.text: Composer produced a rough sound for us to hear

indicators.note: for us to hear means the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: to burr is to make a rough whirring sound or speak with a rolled R

explanation.surface: A composer made a harsh noise for his audience.
explanation.walkthrough: William Byrd was an English Renaissance composer.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was a leading English composer of the Tudor era.

clue.text: Goddess is one attracted to Society

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A goddess is someone drawn to high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egyptian religion.

clue.text: Workers given honour, see, in generous manner

parts.note: hands are manual workers
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Workers awarded an honour, look, are treated generously.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsomely can mean liberally or generously, as in being handsomely rewarded.

clue.text: You will come back to collect when convenient

indicators.note: the reversed word collects the next piece inside it
coming back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: You'll return to pick things up when it suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy can mean undemanding or handy, as in 'at a time easy for you', i.e. convenient.

clue.text: Loud song by good canon may give family entertainment

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an air is a tune or song
a round is a canon, a song sung in overlapping parts

explanation.surface: A loud song with a good canon could entertain the whole family.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground with its rides and stalls is a place of entertainment for families.
